name: Radio e Bluetooth
description: Il lessico delle connessioni senza fili: BLE, RF, reti mesh.

terms.definition: The part of a device that sends and receives radio waves.
terms.example: We moved the antenna away from the battery to improve the range.

terms.definition: Received signal strength indicator: how strong the received radio signal is.
terms.example: The RSSI dropped to minus ninety dBm at ten meters.

terms.definition: Bluetooth Low Energy: a version of Bluetooth designed for very low power.
terms.example: The sensor sends its data over BLE every second.

terms.definition: Short BLE packets a device sends to say it is there and can connect.
terms.example: We reduced the advertising interval to save power.

terms.definition: The BLE structure of services and characteristics used to exchange data.
terms.example: The temperature value is a characteristic in the GATT table.

terms.definition: A single value inside a BLE service, like a temperature reading.
terms.example: The phone writes the new configuration to a characteristic.

terms.definition: The first secure exchange between two Bluetooth devices.
terms.example: Pairing fails if the phone and the device use different security modes.

terms.definition: Saving the pairing keys so the devices can reconnect securely later.
terms.example: After bonding, the watch reconnects automatically.

terms.definition: How often two connected BLE devices exchange packets.
terms.example: A longer connection interval reduces power but increases latency.

terms.definition: The percentage of data packets that never arrive.
terms.example: We measured two percent packet loss in the factory.

terms.definition: Unwanted signals that disturb the radio communication.
terms.example: Wi-Fi interference caused the BLE disconnections.

terms.definition: Changing radio channel continuously to avoid interference.
terms.example: Bluetooth uses channel hopping across forty channels.

terms.definition: Radio bands below one gigahertz, used for long range at low power.
terms.example: The sub-GHz radio reaches two kilometers in open field.

terms.definition: A long-range, low-power radio technology for IoT sensors.
terms.example: The meters send one LoRa message per hour.

terms.definition: A low-power mesh network protocol for smart home devices.
terms.example: The light bulbs form a Zigbee mesh network.

terms.definition: A low-power IP mesh network used by Matter devices.
terms.example: The new sensors join the Thread network automatically.

terms.definition: A standard that lets smart home devices from different brands work together.
terms.example: We are certifying the plug for Matter.

terms.definition: Setting up a new device so it can join the network and the cloud.
terms.example: Wi-Fi provisioning is done with the phone app over BLE.

terms.definition: A network where devices pass messages to each other to cover a large area.
terms.example: In a mesh network, every node can repeat the message.

terms.definition: A device that connects local sensors to the internet.
terms.example: The gateway collects data from fifty sensors.

terms.definition: The total balance of gains and losses on a radio link.
terms.example: The link budget is one hundred and twenty dB.

terms.definition: The weakest signal a receiver can still decode.
terms.example: The receiver sensitivity is minus one hundred and five dBm.

terms.definition: How strong the signal is when it leaves the antenna.
terms.example: We set the transmit power to zero dBm.

terms.definition: Decibels relative to one milliwatt: the unit of radio power.
terms.example: Plus ten dBm is ten milliwatts.

terms.definition: The tests that prove a radio product meets the legal limits.
terms.example: The RF certification took six weeks.

terms.definition: Working well together with other radios in the same band.
terms.example: We tested BLE and Wi-Fi coexistence on the same chip.

terms.definition: A small device that keeps broadcasting a short radio message.
terms.example: The beacon helps the app find the nearest room.

terms.definition: The maximum distance at which the radio link works.
terms.example: The range is fifty meters indoors.

terms.definition: The way data is encoded on the radio wave.
terms.example: LoRa uses a chirp spread spectrum modulation.

terms.definition: The software layers that implement a radio protocol.
terms.example: We updated the BLE stack to fix the connection bug.

terms.definition: Updating the device software through a wireless link.
terms.example: Firmware over the air must not brick the device if the battery dies.

terms.definition: How much data the link can transfer per second.
terms.example: The BLE throughput is about one megabit per second.
